article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 75% Indica / 25% Sativa
Genetics: Super Skunk × Big Skunk Korean × Jack Herer
Breeder: Soma’s Sacred Seeds
THC Content: 18–22%
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , pinene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Mango, tropical fruit, citrus, sweet herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Few cannabis names describe their sensory identity as accurately as Somango . Originally called Soma #5, this tropical cultivar earned its permanent name after its ripe-mango character became impossible to ignore. Soma Seeds developed the plant from a mixture of Jack Herer, Big Skunk Korean, and Super Skunk genetics, producing marijuana that combines vigorous branching and substantial height with the relaxing foundation expected from a 75% indica hybrid.

Yet the experience is far livelier than those numbers might suggest. Somango can be mentally bright, euphoric, and creatively useful without immediately pushing the body into inactivity, while its fragrant flowers combine mango flesh, citrus, herbs, pepper, and unmistakable Skunk depth. The breeder describes it as one of the fruitiest creations in the Soma catalog and specifically emphasizes its uplifting, mentally stimulating effects.
Genetics and Lineage

Somango comes directly from Soma’s Sacred Seeds, and its breeder-supported genetic foundation is Super Skunk, Big Skunk Korean, and Jack Herer. Soma explains the breeding more specifically as the multiple hybrid Jack Herer being combined with Big Skunk Korean, while the official genetic listing also identifies Super Skunk as part of the cultivar’s ancestry. Before its mango aroma inspired the current name, the plant circulated as Soma #5. The breeder classifies the finished variety at approximately 75% indica and 25% sativa.

Each part of that family contributes a recognizable element. Jack Herer brings a complex sativa-influenced background and helps account for the clear, energetic side of the effects. Big Skunk Korean contributes unusual fruit and aromatic depth along with branching vigor, while Super Skunk reinforces density, resin production, earthy sweetness, and traditional cannabis pungency. Together they produce something more tropical and refined than a conventional Skunk cross. Although the plant carries substantial indica influence, its long lateral branches and above-average stretch keep it from behaving like a squat Afghan-style weed plant.
Effects and Experience

Somango often begins in the head rather than the body. The initial shift can feel optimistic and mentally expansive, with colors, music, conversation, or creative work becoming more engaging. Focus can remain surprisingly intact at moderate doses, which helps explain why the breeder promotes the cultivar for socializing and creative activity. Soma specifically describes the effect as euphoric, alert, uplifting, and mentally stimulating rather than a classic couch-lock experience. That distinction makes Somango unusual among heavily indica-leaning hybrids: its genetic classification suggests substantial physical weight, but the opening portion of the high can feel considerably more animated.

Relaxation develops underneath that cerebral lift as time passes. Muscular tension may become less noticeable, the pace of thought tends to smooth out, and the experience eventually becomes calmer without necessarily becoming incapacitating. Larger amounts can shift the balance toward heavier relaxation and sleepiness, particularly for consumers with limited THC tolerance. Potency varies by harvest, but commercial examples are frequently found around the high-teens to low-20% THC range. Because cannabinoid concentration can change considerably between growers and phenotypes, the laboratory label on the actual flower remains more useful than treating any single THC number as universal.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mood elevation and gradual bodily relaxation has made Somango appealing to some medical marijuana consumers seeking relief without immediately becoming heavily sedated. Its brighter early phase may be preferable for people who want cannabis during the afternoon or early evening while remaining functional, while the later calming effect may suit periods of rest. Anecdotally, consumers may choose cultivars with this type of experience when dealing with stress, low mood, mild physical discomfort, appetite issues, or difficulty winding down.

Somango itself, however, has not been established in clinical trials as a treatment for any specific disease. Medical cannabis research generally evaluates cannabinoids, standardized formulations, or broader cannabis preparations rather than named commercial cannabis strains . Responses to THC are also highly individual. Larger doses may increase anxiety, dizziness, impaired attention, dry mouth, or excessive sedation instead of relieving symptoms. Anyone using marijuana for a persistent medical condition should consider the cannabinoid analysis of the specific product and discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Ripe tropical fruit dominates the first impression. A well-cured flower can release an aroma reminiscent of freshly cut mango, sweet orange, fermented fruit, green herbs, and resinous cannabis. Breaking apart the bud generally exposes a stronger Skunk component accompanied by pepper and earthy spice. The contrast keeps Somango from becoming one-dimensional: sweetness sits at the front of the profile, but pungent herbal and skunky notes provide enough depth to prevent it from smelling like artificial fruit candy. Soma credits this unusually tropical aroma and flavor as the reason Soma #5 was ultimately renamed Somango.

The terpene composition of individual batches should always be confirmed through laboratory testing, but myrcene, pinene, limonene, and caryophyllene are commonly associated with examples sold under the name. That combination makes sensory sense. Myrcene can contribute earthy fruit and musk, limonene supports brighter citrus tones, pinene adds fresh herbal sharpness, and caryophyllene fits the peppery background. When smoked or vaporized, mango sweetness tends to appear early, followed by citrus, herbs, and a slightly spicy Skunk finish that remains on the palate.
Growing Information

Somango prefers room to branch. Rather than concentrating most of its production into one central cola, the plant naturally develops long lateral growth and performs especially well when cultivated as a multi-branched specimen. Soma Seeds specifically recommends this approach because the genetics encourage longer side branches and somewhat greater height. Sea of Green cultivation remains possible, but growers need to control both vertical stretch and branching to maintain an even canopy. The breeder favors indoor soil cultivation with organic nutrients, although other growing media can also produce satisfactory plants.

Training early is often more useful than trying to restrain mature plants late in flowering. Topping, low-stress training, or a screen can spread the vigorous branches horizontally and expose additional flowering sites to direct light. Indoor bloom normally lasts nine to ten weeks. As maturity approaches, foliage may begin displaying purple shades while flowers accumulate a thick layer of resin. Soma notes that the trichome coverage is substantial enough to make good finger hash, adding another attraction for growers interested in resin rather than flower weight alone.

Production is better described as moderate than enormous. Soma’s current listing specifies a minimum yield of roughly 25–30 grams but does not provide standardized grams-per-square-meter or outdoor figures, making precise yield claims difficult to justify. Outdoors, plants can become substantially larger when given warmth, direct sun, root space, and a sufficiently long season, with harvest generally falling in October. Dense, resinous flowers require good airflow as autumn humidity rises. Growers who prioritize aroma and trichome quality over maximum bulk are likely to appreciate the cultivar most.
FAQ
Is Somango an indica or sativa?

Somango is an indica-dominant hybrid that Soma Seeds classifies as approximately 75% indica and 25% sativa. Despite that ratio, the high can feel surprisingly cerebral and energetic at first, with physical relaxation becoming more apparent later.
What are the genetics of Somango?

The original Soma Seeds version combines Super Skunk, Big Skunk Korean, and Jack Herer genetics. The breeder describes the principal pairing as Jack Herer with Big Skunk Korean and lists Super Skunk within the complete genetic background.
Is Somango the same strain as Soma #5?
Yes. Soma #5 was the cultivar’s original working name. Its pronounced tropical mango aroma eventually inspired Soma Seeds to rename it Somango.
What does Somango taste like?

Mango is the signature flavor, accompanied by tropical fruit, sweet citrus, herbs, pepper, earth, and Skunk. Some flowers lean heavily toward ripe fruit, while others show more of the herbal and pungent characteristics inherited from the Jack Herer and Skunk side of the lineage.
How long does Somango take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally requires nine to ten weeks according to Soma Seeds. Outdoor plants are usually ready during October in climates capable of supporting the full flowering cycle.
Final Thoughts on Somango

Somango has survived well beyond the era when it was simply known as Soma #5 because it offers something more substantial than an appealing name. Its tropical character is genuinely central to the cultivar, with mango and citrus layered over herbs, pepper, resin, and Skunk. Equally important is the unusual effect profile: an indica-dominant genetic composition produces a high that can begin energetic, social, and creative before settling into a more comfortable physical calm.

In the garden, long branches, moderate yields, purple late-season coloration, and abundant resin give growers several reasons to look beyond raw production numbers. For consumers, the combination of old-school Jack Herer and Skunk ancestry with unusually vivid tropical flavor creates weed that remains recognizable in a market crowded with fruit-named hybrids. Somango is ultimately best suited to enthusiasts who value aroma, clarity of effect, and genetic history as much as maximum THC or oversized yields.
